meta.subtitle: Server 172.16.13.19 - Two Campaigns (256 GB + 128 GB)
meta.platform: Tyrone MDI300 / 2x Intel Xeon 6730P (64C/128T, Granite Rapids)

executive_summary: Two memory configurations were validated back-to-back on the same server 172.16.13.19 (Tyrone MDI300, dual Intel Xeon 6730P Granite Rapids): Campaign A - 8x Samsung 256 GB DDR5-6400 (2 TB); Campaign B - 8x Samsung 128 GB DDR5-6400 (1 TB) after a physical swap.

The memory passes in both campaigns: all 8 modules detected by BMC, BIOS and kernel, trained at full rated 6400 MT/s, with zero ECC errors across a 30-minute pattern-verify pass and a 15-minute >=95%-RAM-resident burn each.

Testing also identified a platform firmware fault: every CPU core is locked at 500 MHz in BOTH campaigns. The lock survived the reboot and DIMM swap - confirming it is independent of the memory. It must be fixed before this server is benchmarked or deployed; bandwidth figures here are throttled ~10x and are not representative.

comparison.notes: Bandwidth is throttled ~10x by the 500 MHz CPU lock and is NOT representative - measured is only ~7-14% of expected. Both campaigns produce nearly identical throttled numbers, further proof the bottleneck is the CPU lock, not the DIMMs. Re-measure after the lock is cleared.

sel_status: BMC SEL: 0 memory-related events. IPMI sees exactly 8 populated DIMM thermal sensors (28-32 C), all 'ok'.
dmesg_status: 0 MCE; EDAC enumerated all 16 controllers, CE=0 / UE=0 in both campaigns. turbostat shows all 64 cores pinned at 500 MHz despite the OS requesting 3.8 GHz (HWP/PERF_CTL ratio 0x26); no thermal or power limit active (29-35 C, 88-139 W vs 250 W cap, CORE_PERF_LIMIT_REASONS=0). dmesg: intel_uncore_frequency_tpmi 'Unsupported minor version' (kernel 6.8 PM support incomplete for Granite Rapids).
findings: Both DIMM sets (8x 256 GB + 8x 128 GB Samsung DDR5-6400) are healthy and fully validated: detected by BMC/BIOS/kernel, trained at full rated 6400 MT/s, zero ECC errors, zero MCE, mlock on all 64 workers.

PLATFORM FAULT: every CPU core is locked at 500 MHz (one-fifth of the 2500 MHz base) in both campaigns. The lock persisted across reboot and DIMM swap - it is a firmware-level condition independent of the memory.

The OS requests 3.8 GHz through every mechanism and the silicon reports it is capable, with no thermal or power limit active - pointing to a BIOS power-profile / config-TDP setting or early-Granite-Rapids pcode/microcode immaturity.
Bandwidth is throttled ~10x by the CPU lock (~23 GB/s aggregate vs ~300+ expected) - recorded for completeness only, not representative of the platform.
recommendations: Memory: cleared for use - both the 256 GB and 128 GB Samsung DDR5-6400 sets pass all correctness and detection checks. No DIMM action required.

Resolve the 500 MHz CPU lock before benchmarking/deployment (in order of likelihood): (a) BIOS power profile -> set Performance / max TDP; (b) update BIOS + Intel microcode (Granite Rapids pcode); (c) check VR / power-delivery telemetry; (d) try a newer kernel (6.11+/HWE) for full PM support.
Re-run the bandwidth suite once cores reach rated frequency - expect ~300+ GB/s aggregate STREAM for this 4-of-8-channel DDR5-6400 layout.
